item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Feb 23 - Mar 1, 2026)
item.description: This week’s roundup covers a wide range of topics, including the architectural limits of etcd, GPU-initiated networking, the nostalgic design of Apple’s breathing lights, and the surprising persistence of floppy disks in transit systems. Cloud, Kubernetes & Infrastructure Why etcd breaks at scale in Kubernetes - A deep dive into the architectural limitations of etcd and how hyperscalers are evolving beyond it. Sympozium (KubeClaw) — Kubernetes-Native Agentic Control Plane / GitHub Repo: A platform for orchestrating AI agents as isolated skill sidecars with ephemeral RBAC.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Feb 16 - 22, 2026)
item.description: This week’s reading list is heavily focused on Kubernetes observability, AI orchestration, and some very handy tools for navigating the modern web. Cloud, Kubernetes & Infrastructure Fatih Koc’s Observability & Infrastructure Series: Kubernetes Security Observability - A guide to establishing effective security observability in your Kubernetes clusters. OpenTelemetry Kubernetes Pipeline - A walkthrough on setting up a robust OpenTelemetry pipeline specifically for Kubernetes. Monitoring with kube-prometheus-stack - A practical tutorial on monitoring using the popular kube-prometheus-stack.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Feb 9 - 15, 2026)
item.description: This week’s roundup features 40 fresh links covering everything from sandboxing AI agents in Kubernetes to benchmarking LLMs in the game Balatro, along with some spicy open-source drama. Cloud & Kubernetes Kubernetes Gateway API Guide / Archive - A complete step-by-step setup guide for the Kubernetes Gateway API. Agent Sandbox - An official Kubernetes SIGs project for sandboxing AI agents. AI Agent Runtimes on GKE / Video - A guide and accompanying video on building secure, scalable, and isolated AI agent runtimes on Google Kubernetes Engine.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Feb 2 - 8, 2026)
item.description: This week is a massive roundup. The AI agent ecosystem is exploding with new tools (and security leaks), while the “privacy & tunneling” toolbox gets a major refill. AI, Agents & Security Moltbook Database Exposure - Wiz reveals a massive breach in “Moltbook” where millions of API keys were exposed. Moltroad - A “Silk Road” for AI agents to list and trade black market items. P*rnhub for Agents - Exactly what it sounds like… but for AI agents.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Jan 26 - Feb 1, 2026)
item.description: While I try to cover everything from budget Kubernetes to BSD tricks, the star of the show this week is of course ClawdBot/MoltBot/OpenClaw. Photo courtesy of Alejandro Martinez :) Cloud & Kubernetes Kubernetes at $2/month - A guide on running a functional Kubernetes cluster for just $2 a month. EmeritOSS Backs MinIO - Chainguard’s EmeritOSS initiative steps in to support MinIO and other “orphaned” open-source projects. Kubernetes GPU Guide - NVIDIA’s official documentation for GPU-accelerated Kubernetes.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Jan 19 - 25, 2026)
item.description: Here is the roundup of links for this week: Cloud & Infrastructure Exe.dev - A service to spin up instant, publicly accessible virtual machines with persistent disks. Zarf - An open-source tool for declarative software delivery into air-gapped and constrained environments. K3s + Sysbox - A guide on using the Sysbox container runtime with K3s. Cloud Native RAG - A walkthrough on building a fully self-hosted Cloud Native RAG stack with embeddings and vectors.

item.title: What Edu is Reading This Week (Nov 23-30 2025)
item.description: What Edu is Reading This Week « This space for rent » :D AI, LLMs & Automation Model Context Protocol (MCP) Introduction: Documentation for the Model Context Protocol, an open standard designed to enable AI agents (LLMs) to interact securely and predictably with external tools, APIs, and data. Jules: The Autonomous Agent CLI Extension / Jules in 90 seconds / Jules GitHub Repo: The official page (and a GitHub repository for a Gemini extension) of Jules, an asynchronous coding sidekick, letting developers delegate long-running tasks.

item.title: My current workflow to create the weekly reading posts
item.description: My current workflow to create the weekly reading posts Here is a breakdown of the simple, automated, and edited workflow I currently follow every week: 1. Capturing and Collecting Links I use Raindrop.io as a Google Chrome extension and mobile app to save the links I found interesting into a dedicated collection named “00-current”. This collection is configured to be the default saving location for all new bookmarks. 2. Processing (Sunday) I export all the bookmarks saved in the “00-current” collection as a .
